manifest.description: A professional Git workbench inside Visual Studio Code.
manifest.capabilities.untrustedWorkspace: Git execution requires a trusted workspace.
manifest.contributes.configuration.title: AlwayGit
manifest.contributes.configuration.prope: Workbench language. Git operation names remain in English. The in-workbench language selector is remembered for this workspace.
Git executable path. Empty uses the built-in Git extension path or PATH.
Visible workbench refresh interval in seconds.
Allow direct Detached HEAD Checkout. Disabled by default; create and switch to a local branch when inspecting historical versions.
Default to pushing missing annotated Tags reachable from the selected branch during Push. The Push dialog can override and remember this choice.
Push a newly created Tag to the selected remote by default. The Create Tag dialog can override and remember this choice.
Default mode selected when opening Reset. The dialog can override and remember Soft, Mixed, or Hard.
Workbench appearance, keyboard and reading preferences shared across windows.
manifest.dockedModeDescription: Open in a movable view in a sidebar or the panel.
manifest.legacyOpenMode: Legacy opening mode. Used only until Workbench Locations is configured.
manifest.workbenchLocationsDescription: Available Workbench locations and the default destination of Open Workbench. Changing this setting preserves Workbench sessions, drafts and live terminals.
manifest.enabledLocationsDescription: Select one or more locations. Secondary Sidebar and Panel entries follow these settings; the Primary Sidebar launcher stays available. Disabling an optional view preserves its session and live terminals for reopening.
manifest.defaultLocationDescription: Destination for Open Workbench. Must be one of the enabled locations.
manifest.copyToEditor: Copy Current State to a New Editor Tab
